brief: A wall clock with hands that turn and tell the time.

requirements.evidence: Single full hex base piece:0,0,0 with cover:0,0,0;full;top forms a flat disc-like clock body; keyhole hanger accessory:0#0,0#0 added on slot 0 provides wall mounting, but no dedicated clock housing or dial markings are present in catalog.

Central pivot simulated by insert:0,0,0;full;top;0 with female socket + male stud (25mm-ins-male) at centre of cover; one hand represented by prop:2 pencil placed on cover top (yaw adjustable via moveProp). No mechanical movement or driven rotation – parts are static 3D-printed plastic; second hand (ruler) could not be placed without PROP_INSIDE clash, leaving only one hand.

No clock face, numerals, or markings available in parts catalog; cannot display accurate time. Build is a symbolic representation only. Configurator enforces mesh/collision rules and cannot provide timekeeping mechanism, and materials/heat/waterproofing requirements are out of scope.

finish.summary: Built minimal wall-clock mockup: hex base + top cover as disc, keyhole hanger for wall mounting, central stud as pivot with pencil as single rotatable hand (yaw-settable). No true turning mechanism or dial exists in Hex Cluster catalog, so time-telling is unmet; second hand omitted due to prop overlap. Mesh clash clear.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

parts.name: Blank plug
parts.use: Fills an insert recess you are not using, so the face reads flat and the pocket stays clean.

parts.name: Female socket
parts.use: Seats in a recess and takes a stud, which makes it the bottom of every stacked insert.

parts.name: Male stud
parts.use: Threads through a seated socket and stands proud of the face, so it can carry whatever mounts above it.

parts.name: Foot
parts.use: Snaps onto a stud to give the face something to stand on, so a cell can rest on its cover rather than on its rim.

parts.name: Zip-tie anchor
parts.use: Seats in a recess and gives a cable tie something to pass through, so a bundle is anchored to the face instead of looped around it.

parts.name: Trinity handle
parts.use: Reaches across a whole triangle of studs, so a lift is shared between recesses instead of hanging off one, and the cell can be carried loaded.
